label: IMMENSE_1: a primitive predicate for being contained by no place and present to everything
definition: PRIMITIVE. Immense g: g is measured or contained by no place and is present to everything that is. After ST I q.8 (God is in all things as an agent is present to what it acts on, and in every place by giving it being). Counterexample: a body, which is contained by its place and absent from other places.
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: typed accounts of place and of an agent's presence to its effect. Distinct from INFINITE_2 (quantitative or spatial infinity of extent): immensity here is not having infinite extent. Two open bridges constrain it, each giving a sufficient condition: 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is IMMENSE_1' and the weaker sense bridge 'Whatever is IMMENSE_2 is IMMENSE_1', from the typed sibling IMMENSE_2 (641c767b: infinite and causes the being of everything else; disambiguation 3fc3ee02). IMMENSE_2 types the grounds, not place, measure or presence by power and knowledge, so the typed account of place and presence remains open.

formal_gap.meaning: Primitives.Immense g says that g is measured or contained by no place and is present to everything that is, as an agent is present to what it acts on (ST I q.8). It is a supplied predicate on beings, one of the Dei Filius ch. 1 attribute primitives. It is not having infinite spatial extent.
formal_gap.examples_unavailable: Presence to everything that is, contained by no place, is claimed only of the being the case investigates; giving an instance would presuppose that conclusion. The record's counterexample (a body, contained by its place and absent from other places) marks its boundary.
exclusions: A body, which is contained by its place and absent from other places.
INFINITE_2, quantitative or spatial infinity of extent.

IMMENSE_2, the typed sibling (infinite and causes the being of everything else): it types grounds, not place, measure or presence, and reaches IMMENSE_1 only by an open sense bridge (Immense disambiguation 3fc3ee02).
open_obligations: No axiom constrains it; two open bridges give sufficient conditions only: 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is IMMENSE_1' and 'Whatever is IMMENSE_2 is IMMENSE_1'.
Typed accounts of place, measure and an agent's presence to its effect are OPEN.
Formalization candidate only after those accounts exist.
